gen_risks.description: Financial management control breakdown due to unretired travel advances and inadequate documentation of eligible expenditures in PFMUs and FPFMD.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an enhanced accountability framework in the Financial Procedures Manual, including strict acquittal rules for travel advances and risk-based internal auditing.
gen_risks.evidence: The key issues noted within the PFMUs and FPFMD are unretired advances and inadequate documentation of the eligible expenditures incurred.

gen_risks.description: Sensitivity of farm enterprise financial viability to reductions in agricultural output market prices.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish business alliances and forward off-take contracts with price-smoothing arrangements, alongside market information platforms to help farmers time sales.
gen_risks.evidence: The project is highly robust to increase in prices of inputs (cost) while being sensitive to a reduction in output prices (benefits).

gen_risks.description: Low procurement implementation capacity and lack of standardized procurement tools across state coordination offices.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit experienced procurement officers and hire an external procurement consultant to build capacity across NCO and SCOs under Bank oversight.
gen_risks.evidence: The procurement capacity is still considered low and most of the states do not have procurement tools in place.

gen_risks.description: Proliferation of adulterated or low-quality seeds, fertilizers, and agro-chemicals in domestic input markets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen capacity of regulatory bodies (Seed Council, Fertilizer Department) for input quality assurance and publish accredited lists of agro-dealers.
gen_risks.evidence: support to FMARD in improving quality control of inputs and information to farmers on input markets and agro-dealers

gen_risks.description: Delays in contract execution caused by high-level pre-determined contract approval thresholds at State Executive Council and Federal Executive Council levels.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish streamlined contract review schedules and engage State Steering Committees early to fast-track contract award approvals.
gen_risks.evidence: approval of contract awards at a pre-determined threshold is the prerogative of the Governor and the State Executive Council

gen_risks.description: Coordination bottlenecks and operational friction across multiple federal and state implementation structures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce standard operating procedures defined in the Project Implementation Manual and conduct joint quarterly technical review meetings.
gen_risks.evidence: inherent risks and issues of multiple implementation levels

gen_risks.description: Delays in project execution during the 18-month competitive recruitment and replacement of existing implementation staff.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain temporary transition arrangements using existing CADP staff while expediting competitive recruitment under World Bank review.
gen_risks.evidence: selection and replacement of CADP staff will be completed, following the agreed selection procedures in compliance with World Bank policies

gen_risks.description: Inability or failure of smallholders and commercial buyers to sustain business alliance contracts and out-grower market linkages.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated technical assistance, business planning support, and third-party facilitation to structure legally sound, mutually beneficial out-grower contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: inability of buyers and sellers to successfully integrate into local, national, and/or international value chains market

gen_risks.description: Persistent gender gaps limiting female farmers' access to land, agricultural inputs, finance, and productive assets.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute a dedicated Women and Youth Empowerment sub-component providing targeted start-up grants, mentorship, and gender tracker monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: women in Nigeria, compared with men, have relatively limited access to productive agricultural land, inputs and services.

gen_risks.description: Soil, surface water, and habitat contamination resulting from agricultural chemical runoffs and small civil works waste.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement the Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF) and Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP) with mandatory site-specific screening.
gen_risks.evidence: The adverse impact could include contamination of soils and surface water, waste generation, dust pollution, disruption in natural habitats

gen_risks.description: Involuntary land acquisition or restriction of common land access caused by infrastructure investments and aggregation center construction.
gen_risks.mitigation: Screen all infrastructure sites using the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) and prepare Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) with full compensation prior to works.
gen_risks.evidence: infrastructure investments could result in involuntary re-settlement and land requisition

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic downturn and state government liquidity crunches caused by national oil price shocks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Structure project financing with 100% IDA funding to eliminate state counterpart funding dependencies and implement performance-based resource allocations.
gen_risks.evidence: The collapse of oil prices and the liquidity crunch revived tensions between federal government and subnational governments

gen_risks.description: Trade policy shifts and cross-border smuggling undermining the market competitiveness of domestic value chain commodities like rice.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage FMARD and Federal Steering Committee in policy dialogue to maintain stable agricultural trade policies and enhance domestic processing quality.
gen_risks.evidence: Erratic protectionist tariffs, which encourage smuggling of rice across borders

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk has been rated Substantial. Coordination of externally funded projects' responsibilities between the federal and state levels is a complex phenomenon, and incomprehension or misinterpretation at any level can affect the project implementation negatively.
gt_risks.mitigation: A communication strategy, supported by the project, will ensure that transparency is maintained at all levels of project management and implementation, and the participation of beneficiaries remains at the core of the project.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risks are rated Substantial. Falling oil prices have undermined economic growth in the country and remain a major source of risks, which may be exacerbated further by security challenges, natural disasters, and climate change. With reliance on a few primary exports and a relatively undiversified economy, Nigeria remains vulnerable to external demand and price shocks, compounded by pressures from weak fiscal management.
gt_risks.mitigation: The World Bank is in close dialogue with the authorities on the reform program in support of restoring macro-economic resilience and economic growth.

gt_risks.description: Sector Policies and Strategies risk has been rated Substantial. One major risk is frequent changes in the agricultural policy, especially the tariff policy, which would change the economic incentives faced by farmers and the private sector alike. Considering this is a multi-sector project, risk associated with other sector policies (e.g., transport and energy) might also affect implementation.
gt_risks.mitigation: These risks will be mitigated through a sustained, evidence-based policy dialogue and engagement with the government to ensure sustainability of the reforms in the sector.

gt_risks.description: Technical Design risk has been rated Moderate. The approach for agribusiness partnership proposed by this project has already been successfully implemented under CADP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Lessons learned from both CADP and other similar operations have been incorporated into the project design, which is based on analyses undertaken during preparation and summarized under Annex 2.

gt_risks.description: Institutional Capacity for Implementation and Sustainability risk has been rated Substantial. While capacity at the federal level for implementing World Bank-supported agricultural project activities is adequate, there is a risk at state level of insufficient experience, structure, and technical knowhow to manage the new project design features.
gt_risks.mitigation: SCOs' staff will be provided necessary training at the time of launching the project, and newly recruited staff (particularly in Kogi state) will benefit from an induction training program. Coordination challenges will be addressed by Steering Committees at federal and state levels, and a Technical Committee at state level chaired by the Commissioner of Agriculture. NCO and SCO will collaborate with FADAMAIII, RAMP, and GEM where relevant, and the project may contract a third-party service provider to assist states in project execution.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (financial management) is assessed as Substantial. The key risks identified are those of value for money in works/construction contracts and capacity building events; capacity building activities such as training workshops have been identified as having significant fiduciary risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: Additional steps include: (i) all training and workshop activities subject to prior review by the Bank; (ii) activities part of the approved annual work plan; (iii) part of the project training plan; and (iv) compliance with the enhanced accountability framework. A qualified procurement specialist will be selected competitively; goods and consultants' services will be procured in accordance with World Bank anti-fraud/corruption guidelines and procurement guidelines.

gt_risks.description: Environment and Social risk has been rated Substantial. The Environmental Category assigned to the project is Category B, predicated on the assumption that environmental risks and social impact may not have serious adverse impact of a sensitive or diverse nature; the project may not be engaged in development of heavy infrastructure or acquisition of large expanses of land.
gt_risks.mitigation: An Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and an Integrated Pest Management Plan (IPMP) have been prepared and publicly disclosed. Specific Environment and Social Impact Assessments (ESIAs) and Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) will be conducted for each public and private investment once the type of work is determined and precisely located, and a Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment will cover all areas and localities in which the project will operate.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholders/Gender risk: there is a risk that women will be disadvantaged in terms of their access to employment and participation in out-growers arrangements.
gt_risks.mitigation: A detailed gender assessment and tracking for the project will be undertaken with the DFID-supported Gender Filter Trust Fund, in collaboration with the Africa Gender Innovation Lab, and incorporated into the Project Implementation Manual. A substantial part of Component 2 (35% of project funding) will support a Women and Youth Empowerment program, with affirmation of 35 percent female inclusion in all aspects of the project (representation in joint community meetings, jobs, extension agents, facilitators, and agri-business/entrepreneurship development), plus TA and training on business plan preparation, accounting, and financial management for women.
